title.narrative: Improved fundamental principles and rights at work framework and increased comprehensive programmes to adopt inclusive learning options in line with the challenges of the future of work

description.narrative:
The ILO is committed to strengthening labour rights in Brazil, with a focus on promoting Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work (FPRW), particularly combating child and forced labour and improving occupational safety and health.
In partnership with the federal government, social partners, and the justice system, the ILO is supporting the revision and adoption of National Plans to eradicate child and forced labour. It is also assisting in redesigning PETI, Brazil’s national programme against child labour, and developing a national assistance flow for victims, to be institutionalized via the National Commissions on Child and Forced Labour. In Mato Grosso do Sul, efforts are underway to adopt a new state plan and a protocol for assisting forced labour victims, strengthening local governance and service delivery.
To promote decent work in supply chains (Output 8.4), the federal government is implementing the Decent Work Pact in Rural Areas. In Minas Gerais, municipal governments are working with rural workers’ and coffee producers’ unions to promote formalization, labour rights, and better conditions in the coffee chain. Activities include training, improved labour inspection coordination, and awareness campaigns targeting seasonal and informal workers.
In Pará, rural workers in Terra Roxa are developing a model to improve food security and generate income, helping prevent forced labour. At the national level, the ILO supports Brazil’s pathfinder status under Alliance 8.7 and helps strengthen institutional coordination and strategic planning to eliminate these violations.
These actions support SDG targets 8.7 and 8.4, advancing integrated responses to child and forced labour and promoting decent work and sustainability in rural supply chains.
